entities.name: PMID:25447298
observations: Brown Norway rats received subcutaneous oxytocin (0.02, 0.1, or 0.5 mg/kg) during conditioned taste-aversion training; oxytocin enhanced weak latent inhibition dose-dependently by reducing aversion in pre-exposed rats, with 0.02 mg/kg strongest.
The authors stated that oxytocin facilitation of latent inhibition was consistent with antipsychotic-drug effects.

entities.name: Oxytocin
observations: Peripherally administered subcutaneously in Brown Norway rats at 0.02, 0.1, and 0.5 mg/kg in a latent-inhibition conditioned taste-aversion paradigm.
Enhanced latent inhibition, with the strongest effect at 0.02 mg/kg, according to PMID:25447298.

entities.name: Latent inhibition
observations: Brown Norway rats naturally displayed attenuated latent inhibition; peripheral oxytocin strengthened the pre-exposure effect by reducing conditioned taste aversion in pre-exposed animals.
The direction of modulation was described as consistent with antipsychotic drugs.
